answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by grading each identity's work with a jury drawn from unrelated clusters, so an attacker can never grade its own fakes. Like a lotus rooted far from the jetty where one owner's boats all dock, jurors are picked by distance in the trust graph, never from the submitter's own neighborhood. An attacker who tries to wander into many juries must build standing in dozens of independent groups, and each fake still faces random non-kin graders who lose reputation for approving fraud. The cost grows with every fake, while a lone honest agent pays nothing extra.
